clue.text: Came to a head, say, and created annoyance

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for a past-tense verb: stirred up irritation

indicators.note: 'say' asks for a word that is spoken the same as the phrase before it, not spelt the same

parts.note: to come to a head is to reach a peak

explanation.surface: A boil or quarrel came to a head and caused irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: PEAKED and PIQUED are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique is to irritate or offend, so having piqued someone is having stirred annoyance in them.

clue.text: At home, Electra was weaving twine

indicators.note: weaving twists strands into a new pattern, so the name is rearranged

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: Electra sits at home weaving twine, a tragic heroine at her loom.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist things together, which is what interlacing threads or fingers does.

clue.text: Originally under pressure, foundation to move away

indicators.note: 'Originally' points to the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A house under pressure from subsidence must be moved off its foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot oneself is to leave a settled home and relocate elsewhere.

clue.text: Dog for a countryman

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a native of Dalmatia on the Croatian coast

explanation.surface: A farmer wants a dog to help on the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'countryman' suggests a rustic, but here it means a native of a particular region, Dalmatia.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted breed is named after Dalmatia, and an inhabitant of that region shares the name.

clue.text: Mistakenly, hero to cause alarm

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for a noun: the answer is a device that raises alarm

indicators.note: a mistaken arrangement means the letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A hero mistakenly raises the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooter is a siren or horn, something sounded to give warning.

clue.text: Animal's joint work setback

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the word for work is read in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An animal suffers a setback with its joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the crossword's usual word for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a large African animal.

clue.text: Shade's extremely rudimentary for the glasshouse

parts.note: orange is a shade of colour

indicators.note: 'extremely' means at the extremes, so only the end letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: The shading in this greenhouse is extremely basic.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-walled building originally for growing orange trees, a kind of greenhouse.

clue.text: Former model and artist, an actor

explanation.surface: A one-time fashion model and artist has taken up acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is T from the Ford Model T car; RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is a standard artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer hired for a non-speaking background part in a film or play.

clue.text: Delight in the tenth rally of the season

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A sports fan is thrilled by the tenth rally of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or charm someone, giving them delight.

clue.text: Unhappily, ten pester my parent, whose now childless

indicators.note: something done unhappily is disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ten children pestered their parent for years and have now all left home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'whose' where 'who's' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty nester is a parent whose grown-up children have moved out of the family home.

clue.text: Farmer's ploy: first time, show hesitation

parts.note: a ploy is a scheme or plan

indicators.note: 'first' takes just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A farmer's tactic for the first time is to show some hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter is someone who plants crops, especially one running a plantation.

clue.text: Enthuses in a musical way

parts.note: surface reading: talks excitedly about something
setter's reading: the verb is built on the name of a free-form musical composition

explanation.walkthrough: A rhapsody is a free, emotional piece of music, so the verb for gushing enthusiasm doubles as making music.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhapsodise is to speak or write with great enthusiasm, a word derived from the musical rhapsody.

clue.text: Arrange nap, son, to unsettle unwelcome guest

indicators.note: to unsettle is to disturb, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A parent arranges a nap for their son to calm an unwanted visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'unsettle' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is Latin for an unacceptable person, used of someone no longer welcome.

clue.text: Time for the class of 2000, for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cohort of students who start or finish together

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a reunion; the second meaning is a school or university intake.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a span of twelve months and also a group of pupils in the same school grade.

clue.text: Gale damages the hedges

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A storm has damaged the garden hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedges are often planted as shelter belts to block the wind.

clue.text: Inaction caused by wayward English dude eating fat

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself
wayward means straying off course, so the letters go out of order

explanation.surface: A lazy Englishman's idleness comes from eating too much fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inaction' is a fair definition because desuetude is a formal word for disuse, the state of no longer being active.
explanation.definitionFit: Desuetude is a state of disuse, so it means inactivity.

clue.text: Get garage to reassemble the combination

indicators.note: reassembling puts parts back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting a garage to rebuild an engine assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a whole formed by bringing several things together, a sum or total.

clue.text: Scattering said to go back to part of Royal Academy, initially

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the word is read backwards
'initially' asks for the starting letter of each word

parts.note: opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Scattered works said to be returning to a section of the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers all four words before it, not just Royal Academy, which could tempt a solver toward RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people from their homeland, a scattering.

clue.text: Viewer to see humour displayed by US agent Eliot

parts.note: to eye is to look at
Eliot Ness led the Untouchables against Al Capone

explanation.surface: A viewer watches Eliot Ness show his humour on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot Ness was the Prohibition agent famous from The Untouchables.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who saw an event with their own eyes, an onlooker.

clue.text: Penned in, about to go off the older generation

definitions.note: the answer is used with 'the' as a plural noun for old people

indicators.note: going off means departing, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: penned in means confined, as in a cage

explanation.surface: The elderly feel penned in and about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, about) is taken out of CAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: The aged is a collective term for elderly people, the senior generation.

clue.text: Sound building

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a building where horses are kept

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it describes a solid structure; apart, it is an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and firm, and a stable is the shelter that houses horses.

clue.text: Artless head has the quality of being clear

parts.note: an artless person is open and transparent

explanation.surface: An innocent leader has a clear, honest character.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland, a common element in British place names such as Inverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparentness is the state of being see-through, clarity.

clue.text: No time for loudspeaker to irritate

indicators.note: 'No' means doing without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand of public-address loudspeaker

explanation.surface: A noisy loudspeaker with no time to spare is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannoy is the British trade name for a public-address system; T is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate or bother them.

clue.text: Concur that article's almost Green

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a newspaper article is almost environmentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, to agree.

clue.text: Went on about our hard feelings

parts.note: a bus that ran went on its route

explanation.surface: Someone went on and on about their resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, lasting resentment, the same as hard feelings.

clue.text: Conductor's indications to cheerful old Bob?

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A conductor signals to a happy old man called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was British slang for a shilling, a pre-decimal coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeats are the unaccented beats a conductor marks with an upward movement of the baton.

clue.text: Spin good yarn, initially to order

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the starting letters of the words just before

parts.note: to rate is to rank or order

explanation.surface: Spinning good yarn to fill an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' and 'yarn' suggest a story or spinning wool; spin is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to rotate or whirl around, to spin.

clue.text: Oral agreement to allow a small hole

indicators.note: 'Oral' means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: aye is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A verbal agreement to allow a small hole to be made.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small round hole for a lace or cord to pass through.
